decisive_moments.reason: Con directly reframed the burden around whether benchmarks deserve primacy across broad AI progress, rather than merely whether they are useful. It identified production properties—security, reliability, latency, cost, maintainability, and distribution shift—that public capability scores systematically omit.

Pro offered a coherent layered model and addressed developer freedom and user protection, but largely treated production evaluations as add-ons while retaining benchmark primacy. It did not establish why prototype-oriented comparability should dominate coordination for production systems.

Con clearly distinguished narrow capability research from production-system progress and explained why contextual, evolving properties require pluralistic evaluation. It also acknowledged benchmark value, avoiding an overclaim that benchmarks are useless.

flags.quote: Public evaluation also protects users by exposing weaknesses before deployment
Public benchmarks should therefore remain the anchor
they cannot make a public benchmark both stable enough for coordination and representative of changing real-world risks
